overview.title: Packing IMDb reviews for RoBERTa
overview.main_topic: Converting raw IMDb review strings into the exact input format RoBERTa saw during pretraining, `<s> tokens </s> <pad>...`, using KerasHub's `StartEndPacker` inside a `tf.data` map, and inspecting a resulting batch.
overview.central_idea: A pretrained model works best when inputs mimic its pretraining format. Listing 15.21 tokenizes each batch of reviews, adds start/end tokens, truncates or pads to 512 tokens, and returns `token_ids` plus a boolean `padding_mask`, the two inputs the RoBERTa backbone expects.
overview.importance: This is the bridge between the raw datasets of p.482 and the fine-tuning on p.485. Getting the packing and the padding mask right determines whether the pretrained representations are usable.
learning_objectives: Explain RoBERTa's sequence packing format and why matching it matters.
Describe what `StartEndPacker` does: add start/end tokens, truncate, pad, and optionally return a padding mask.
Trace the shapes in Listing 15.21 from a batch of 16 strings to two (16, 512) tensors.
Read the printed batch: identify `<s>`=0, `</s>`=2, `<pad>`=1 and tell truncated reviews from padded ones.
Explain why the padding mask is needed.
prerequisites: RoBERTa tokenizer and backbone loaded with KerasHub (p.480)

summary:
The page opens with the example promised at the end of p.482. RoBERTa saw every pretraining sequence as `<s>`, the tokens, `</s>`, then `<pad>` tokens up to a fixed length. Two toy sequences of length 8 show this: "the quick brown fox jumped ." fills the length exactly, and "the panda slept ." is padded with two `<pad>` tokens.

The authors stress matching pretraining's token ordering as closely as possible; the model then trains faster and more accurately. KerasHub's **`StartEndPacker`** layer does this: it appends start, end and padding tokens and trims long sequences to a given length.

**Listing 15.21** defines `preprocess(text, label)`. It creates a `StartEndPacker` with `sequence_length=512` and the tokenizer's own start, end and pad token ids, and asks it to also return a padding mask. It applies `packer(tokenizer(text))` and returns a dict `{"token_ids": ..., "padding_mask": ...}` plus the unchanged label. The dict keys match the backbone's two named inputs (p.481). The function is mapped over the train, validation and test datasets.

**One preprocessed batch** has `token_ids` of shape **(16, 512)** (int32) and `padding_mask` of shape (16, 512) (bool), with labels of shape (16,). Every row begins with **0** (`<s>`). Rows ending in `1, 1, 1` are short reviews padded with `<pad>` = 1, and their mask ends in `False`. Rows ending in `..., 2` are long reviews truncated to 512 tokens and closed by `</s>` = 2, with an all-`True` mask. The page ends with the inputs ready for fine-tuning (p.484).

paragraphs.excerpt: It’s important to match the token ordering used for pretraining as closely as possible;
paragraphs.what_it_says: Matching the token ordering used in pretraining helps the model train faster and more accurately. KerasHub's `StartEndPacker` layer does this packing: it adds start, end and padding tokens and truncates long sequences to a given length. The authors use it with the tokenizer.
paragraphs.what_it_means: The pretrained weights have adapted to a specific input distribution. Position 0 always held `<s>`, a `</s>` always closed the text, and `<pad>` positions were masked out. RoBERTa's learned position embeddings and attention patterns expect this layout. Feeding the same structure means fine-tuning only has to learn the task, not also adapt to a new input format. In particular, the representation at position 0 (`<s>`) is later used as the pooled summary for classification (p.484), so it must really be the start token.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: Small format mismatches (missing `<s>`, wrong pad id, no mask) rarely crash anything but quietly degrade accuracy. A library layer configured from the tokenizer's own ids removes that risk.
paragraphs.technical_idea: Packing = tokenize → truncate to `sequence_length - 2` content tokens → prepend start id → append end id → right-pad with pad id → mask = (position is not padding). The exact truncation rule is a library detail; the printed batch shows truncated rows still end with `</s>` (id 2).

concepts.name: Sequence packing with special tokens
concepts.definition: Formatting each tokenized text as `<s>` + tokens + `</s>`, then padding to a fixed length, exactly as during pretraining.
concepts.intuition: Putting a letter in the envelope the post office's machines are built for.
concepts.technical: For RoBERTa: start id 0, pad id 1, end id 2 (visible in the printed batch). Length fixed at 512.
concepts.significance: Matching the pretraining format lets fine-tuning train faster and more accurately, as the book says.
concepts.misconception: That special tokens are cosmetic. The model's representations, especially at position 0, depend on them.

concepts.name: Padding mask
concepts.definition: A boolean tensor, the same shape as `token_ids`, that is True for real tokens and False for padding.
concepts.intuition: A sticky note marking which seats are empty so nobody tries to talk to them.
concepts.technical: The backbone uses it so attention ignores `<pad>` positions as keys. Without it, real tokens would mix in information from hundreds of pad embeddings in short reviews.
concepts.significance: Lets variable-length reviews share a fixed (16, 512) batch shape without corrupting the representations.
concepts.example: Row 1 of the printed batch: `[True, True, True, ..., False, False, False]`, a short review.
concepts.misconception: That pad id 1 alone is enough. The model needs the explicit mask (passed as an input here); it does not infer padding from the id.

concepts.name: Truncation to the maximum sequence length
concepts.definition: Cutting token sequences longer than `sequence_length` so they fit the model's fixed number of positions.
concepts.intuition: Reading only the first two pages of a long review.
concepts.technical: `sequence_length=512` matches RoBERTa base's maximum number of learned positions. Long reviews keep their first ~510 tokens, and `</s>` is still placed at the end.
concepts.significance: Bounds memory and compute ($O(n^2)$ attention); some information from very long reviews is lost.
concepts.example: Printed row 2 ends `..., 101, 24, 2`: a truncated review, all-True mask.
concepts.misconception: That truncated reviews lose their end token. The printout shows they still end with id 2.

code.title: RoBERTa packing format (illustration)
code.what_it_does: Shows two token sequences of length 8 packed as RoBERTa expects: start token, content, end token, then padding.

line_explanations.explanation: Six content tokens + `<s>` + `</s>` = 8, filling the length exactly; no padding.
Four content tokens + 2 special tokens = 6, so two `<pad>` tokens fill the remaining slots. The `</s>` comes before the padding, not at position 7.

code.inputs_outputs: Illustrative strings; in practice these would be integer ids (0, ..., 2, 1, 1).
code.algorithm: Prepend start, append end, right-pad to fixed length.
code.theory_link: Matches the pretraining input layout so the pretrained weights see familiar inputs.

parameters.name: sequence length
parameters.role: 8 in this toy example; 512 in Listing 15.21.

pitfalls: Real RoBERTa tokens are byte-level BPE pieces (often with a leading-space marker), not whole lowercase words; the example is simplified for readability.

code.title: Preprocessing IMDb movie reviews with RoBERTa's tokenizer
code.original_code:
def preprocess(text, label):
    packer = keras_hub.layers.StartEndPacker(
        sequence_length=512,
        start_value=tokenizer.start_token_id,
        end_value=tokenizer.end_token_id,
        pad_value=tokenizer.pad_token_id,
        return_padding_mask=True,
    )
    token_ids, padding_mask = packer(tokenizer(text))
    return {"token_ids": token_ids, "padding_mask": padding_mask}, label
preprocessed_train_ds = train_ds.map(preprocess)
preprocessed_val_ds = val_ds.map(preprocess)
preprocessed_test_ds = test_ds.map(preprocess)
code.what_it_does: Defines a `tf.data` mapping function that tokenizes a batch of reviews with RoBERTa's tokenizer, packs them to 512 tokens with start/end/pad tokens, and returns the backbone's input dict plus the label; applies it to the three datasets.

line_explanations.explanation: `preprocess` receives one element of the batched dataset: `text` is a (16,) string tensor and `label` a (16,) int tensor (batch size 16 from p.482).

Build the packer. `sequence_length=512` is the fixed output length. `start_value`, `end_value`, `pad_value` come from the tokenizer itself (0, 2, 1 for RoBERTa), so they always match pretraining. `return_padding_mask=True` makes the layer also return the boolean mask.
`tokenizer(text)` yields a ragged batch of token ids (each review has a different length); `packer(...)` turns it into dense (16, 512) `token_ids` and (16, 512) `padding_mask`.
Return `(inputs, label)`. The dict keys must exactly match the backbone's input names `token_ids` and `padding_mask` (p.481) so Keras routes them correctly.
Lazily map the function over train, validation and test sets. Preprocessing runs on the fly in the input pipeline (on CPU) during training and evaluation.

code.inputs_outputs: In: (text: string[16], label: int[16]). Out: ({"token_ids": int32[16, 512], "padding_mask": bool[16, 512]}, label: int[16]).
code.algorithm: Tokenize → pack (start + truncated tokens + end + pads) → mask = not pad.
code.theory_link: Implements the 'matching tokenizer' requirement (pp.479-480) and the pretraining packing format; the padding mask lets attention ignore padding.

parameters.name: sequence_length=512
parameters.role: Fixed length; RoBERTa base's maximum number of positions. Longer reviews are truncated.

parameters.name: start_value / end_value / pad_value
parameters.role: Special-token ids taken from the tokenizer so they match pretraining.

parameters.name: return_padding_mask
parameters.role: If True, also return the boolean mask the backbone needs.

pitfalls: The packer is constructed inside `preprocess`. Under `ds.map` the function is traced once into a graph, so this is cheap; calling `preprocess` eagerly in a loop would rebuild the layer each time. Creating the packer once outside the function is the more conventional pattern.

512 tokens for every review is costly: attention is quadratic in length and many reviews are much shorter. Dynamic padding or a smaller length would be faster at some cost in accuracy on long reviews.
Without `.prefetch()` / `num_parallel_calls`, tokenization may bottleneck GPU training (beyond the book).
If the dict keys differ from the backbone input names, Keras raises an error or misroutes inputs.
code.illustrative_code:
# AI-written sketch, not from the book: same pipeline with the packer built once and parallel mapping
packer = keras_hub.layers.StartEndPacker(
    sequence_length=512,
    start_value=tokenizer.start_token_id,
    end_value=tokenizer.end_token_id,
    pad_value=tokenizer.pad_token_id,
    return_padding_mask=True,
)
def preprocess(text, label):
    token_ids, padding_mask = packer(tokenizer(text))
    return {"token_ids": token_ids, "padding_mask": padding_mask}, label
preprocessed_train_ds = train_ds.map(preprocess, num_parallel_calls=tf.data.AUTOTUNE).prefetch(tf.data.AUTOTUNE)

deeper.title: Reading the special-token ids from the printout
deeper.body:
The printed batch identifies RoBERTa's special-token ids without any documentation:

- Column 0 is always **0**, so `<s>` = 0 (`start_token_id`).
- Padded rows end in **1** wherever the mask is False, so `<pad>` = 1 (`pad_token_id`).
- Rows with an all-True mask end in **2**, so `</s>` = 2 (`end_token_id`).

The all-True rows are reviews with at least ~510 subword tokens. Since many IMDb reviews are a few hundred words long, both cases appear in a batch of 16.

deeper.title: Why the mask matters numerically
deeper.body: Take a review of 120 tokens (122 with `<s>`/`</s>`) padded to 512: 390 of 512 positions (76%) are padding. Without a mask, each real token's softmax attention would spread over 512 keys, most of them identical pad embeddings, diluting the real context; the `<s>` vector used for classification (p.484) would be mostly an average of padding. With the mask, attention logits for pad keys are set to a very large negative number before the softmax, giving them weight effectively 0, so the 122 real tokens attend only to each other.

deeper.title: Analogy: a standard form
deeper.body: RoBERTa was trained on forms that always start with a header box (`<s>`), contain text, end with a signature line (`</s>`), and leave unused lines blank and marked 'N/A' (pad + mask). Filling in your IMDb reviews on the same form lets the clerk (the pretrained network) process them at once, instead of first having to learn a new layout.

misconceptions.claim: The chapter 14 IMDb vectorizer can be reused to tokenize inputs for RoBERTa.
misconceptions.correction: The ids must come from RoBERTa's own tokenizer and be packed in its pretraining format (`<s>` ... `</s>` `<pad>`), as in Listing 15.21.

misconceptions.claim: The padding mask is optional because padding uses a dedicated token id.
misconceptions.correction: The backbone takes `padding_mask` as an explicit input (p.481); it is what tells attention to ignore pad positions.

misconceptions.claim: Truncated reviews lose their end token.
misconceptions.correction: `StartEndPacker` still places `</s>` (id 2) at the end; see the rows ending in `..., 2` with all-True masks.

misconceptions.claim: `token_ids` row values like 713 are words in the chapter 14 vocabulary.
misconceptions.correction: They are RoBERTa BPE subword ids from a vocabulary of about 50,000 (p.480).

takeaways: RoBERTa expects `<s>` tokens `</s>` followed by `<pad>`s; matching this makes fine-tuning faster and more accurate.
`StartEndPacker` adds start/end tokens, truncates or pads to 512, and can return a padding mask, using the tokenizer's own special ids.
`preprocess` returns a dict whose keys match the backbone's inputs: `token_ids` and `padding_mask`.
A batch has `token_ids` and `padding_mask` of shape (16, 512) and labels of shape (16,).
In the printout, 0 = `<s>`, 2 = `</s>`, 1 = `<pad>`; all-True mask rows are truncated long reviews.

questions.question: What does `StartEndPacker` NOT do in Listing 15.21?
options: Convert raw text into token ids
questions.answer: Convert raw text into token ids
questions.explanation: Tokenization is done by `tokenizer(text)`; the packer receives the ids. The book says the packer appends start, end and padding tokens and trims long sequences to a given length.

questions.question: From the printed batch, what are the token ids of <s>, </s> and <pad> in RoBERTa?
questions.explanation: Every row starts with 0; padded rows end with 1s where the mask is False; full rows end with 2.

questions.question: Why do the authors insist on matching the token ordering used during pretraining?
questions.answer: The pretrained weights (position embeddings, attention patterns, the meaning of position 0) were learned for that format; matching it means fine-tuning only has to learn the task, so the model trains more quickly and accurately.
questions.explanation: The book states the speed and accuracy benefit; the mechanism is that the inputs stay in the distribution the weights were trained on.

questions.question: A row of `padding_mask` is all True. What does that tell you about the review?
options: It had at least enough tokens to fill 512 positions and was truncated
questions.answer: It had at least enough tokens to fill 512 positions and was truncated
questions.explanation: No padding means the packed sequence is full; the matching `token_ids` rows end with `</s>` = 2 after real content. Sentiment is unrelated, and an empty review would be mostly padding.

questions.question: Why must the keys of the dict returned by `preprocess` be exactly "token_ids" and "padding_mask"?
questions.answer: They are the names of the RoBERTa backbone's two input layers, and Keras routes dict inputs to model inputs by name.
questions.explanation: See the backbone summary on p.481.

questions.question: A review tokenizes to 200 subword tokens. After packing to 512, how many positions are padding, and what fraction of the padding_mask is True?
questions.answer: 200 + 2 special tokens = 202 real positions; 512 − 202 = 310 padding positions; 202/512 ≈ 39.5% True.

questions.question: Could you write `preprocess` from memory and explain each argument of `StartEndPacker`?
questions.answer: sequence_length (512), start_value/end_value/pad_value from the tokenizer, return_padding_mask=True; return ({token_ids, padding_mask}, label).
questions.explanation: If you can also explain the printed batch, you understand the input contract of the pretrained backbone.
